scope: Original 2020 Dune: Imperium base/core standard 2–4-player multiplayer, including required two-player House Hagal; no solo, optional variants, expansions, promos, or Uprising.

verdict.answer_key: One timing inconsistency requiring correction (Q21); other 58 expected answers substantively supported within their questions; one minor wording caveat (Q35).

methodology: Read the complete main-rulebook extraction, icon glossary, Board Space Guide, and general/two-player House Hagal material; solo-only procedures excluded from conclusions.
Read all four pages of the January 13, 2025 official FAQ, selecting original-base applicable entries and excluding expansion/Uprising examples and rules.
Compared every frozen question and expected answer, and challenged the ledger passage-to-question mappings instead of treating a page reference as evidence that every rule on that page is tested.

Cross-checked PDF text for setup and every Board Space Guide/House Hagal entry. Visually rendered and inspected the Sell Melange graphic from PDF p18 in memory, confirming 2/3/4/5 spice buys 6/8/10/12 Solari.
Did not read any project summary, reader response, or grade artifact. Wrote only this review report.

findings.finding: Q21 retains the old rulebook exception for a Conflict-reward Mentat kept through Recall. The official FAQ moves receipt of the Sort Through the Chaos Mentat to the start of the next round, as Q39 correctly states. The winner therefore does not already hold this reward during the preceding Recall.
findings.problematic_expected_text: Non-ending Recall return Mentat to Landsraad except Conflict-reward Mentat kept next round
findings.source_rule: Main p13 normally returns the Mentat during Recall; FAQ p4 Sort Through the Chaos says the winner takes the Mentat at the start of the next round, correcting the p16 immediate-award/retention description.
findings.suggested_correction: Round Start reveals the next Conflict and each human draws five. During non-ending Recall return any currently held/deployed Mentat to its Landsraad space, recall Agents, and pass first player clockwise. If the previous Conflict awarded Sort Through the Chaos, give its winner the Mentat at the start of the next round.
findings.grading_implication: Do not require an answer to repeat the obsolete retention exception or penalize a reader who follows FAQ timing. Keep Q39’s next-round timing.

findings.finding: The ledger maps FAQ Foldspace to Q26, but Q26 asks only the board-space cost/effects and its key only says acquire Foldspace to discard. Neither Q26 nor Q08 asks the distinct prohibition on acquiring Foldspace with ordinary Persuasion.

FAQ p2 Dispatch an Envoy is missing from the ledger and all frozen questions. The general no-icon-removal/no-duplicate-icon ruling applies to the base Intrigue even though the FAQ illustration uses expansion cards.

Q06 only asks about recruits from the board space and played card. The ledger maps FAQ troops to it, but neither the question nor expected answer tests the FAQ’s any-source recruitment rule (including an Intrigue played during the same Combat-space turn) or the explicit ban on re-recruiting garrison troops to evade the two-old-troop deployment cap.

Q35’s expected answer says keep face up until next Reveal that round while also allowing play during a Reveal. Read this as the current Reveal if already taking it; otherwise it risks suggesting a delay beyond the current turn. This is a wording caveat, not a separate substantive rule error.
findings.suggested_correction: May play on own Agent or Reveal turn. If awaiting the applicable Reveal, leave face up; use and discard during that Reveal, including the current Reveal when played there.

proposed_additions.question: May you spend ordinary Reveal-turn Persuasion to buy a Foldspace card from the Reserve, or must an acquisition effect specifically show the Foldspace icon?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Ordinary Persuasion cannot acquire Foldspace. You may acquire it only through a Foldspace-icon effect, such as the Foldspace board space; ordinary Reveal purchases are Imperium Row cards, Arrakis Liaison, and The Spice Must Flow.
proposed_additions.novelty: Specific acquisition eligibility exception. Q08 covers purchasing procedure and Q26 covers the Foldspace board reward but neither asks or requires the prohibition.

proposed_additions.question: After Dispatch an Envoy adds the four Faction Agent icons to a card that already has City and Fremen, do you retain City, and do you now have two Fremen icons?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Retain City and the original Fremen icon. Add only the missing Faction icons; Dispatch an Envoy removes no original icons and creates no duplicate of an icon already present.
proposed_additions.novelty: Omitted named base-card FAQ rule about icon preservation and set-like addition. General matching-icon legality in Q04 does not test it.

proposed_additions.question: On a turn when you send an Agent to a Combat space, may troops recruited by a Plot Intrigue that turn deploy along with the space/card recruits? May you count an existing garrison troop as recruited again to bypass the limit of two additional garrison troops?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Any troop actually recruited that turn from any source, including an Intrigue, may deploy; you may additionally deploy at most two existing garrison troops. Recruitment takes a troop from supply, so you cannot re-recruit a garrison troop to bypass that cap.
proposed_additions.novelty: Tests the explicit any-source scope and anti-re-recruit boundary in FAQ p4. Q06’s board/card arithmetic does not cover either distinction.

proposed_additions.question: You must draw three cards but your deck has only one left and you have a nonempty discard pile. What do you draw, when do you shuffle, and do cards still face up in play enter that shuffle?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Draw the remaining deck card, then when another card must be drawn shuffle your discard into a new deck and continue the draw. Cards still in play stay there until Reveal cleanup unless trashed and are not in the discard shuffle.
proposed_additions.novelty: Direct normal exhausted-deck procedure. Q16 asks only whether inspection permits an early shuffle; Q55 concerns Refocus’s separate empty-discard exception. Neither requires the normal reshuffle operation or its timing within a multi-card draw.

proposed_additions.question: How do you prepare the humans’ initial decks, the Imperium Row, the Intrigue deck, the Reserve, the Mentat and Alliance tokens, and the initial first player before Round 1?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Each human shuffles their own standard ten-card starting deck and places it face down. Shuffle the Imperium deck and deal five face up to the Row; shuffle Intrigues face down separately. Place Arrakis Liaison, The Spice Must Flow, and Foldspace as three separate Reserve stacks beside the Row. Put the Mentat at its Landsraad space and the four Alliances on their marked Influence-track areas. Randomly choose the initial first player and give that player the marker.
proposed_additions.novelty: Initial setup procedure, not component-count trivia. Q01 covers Conflict-deck construction, Q02 covers starting units/resources/Influence/VP, and Q21 starts an already prepared game; none asks how the initial card supplies or initial first player are established.

S01.passages: Setup A1/A2, C1/C2/C3, E and H: Mentat, Alliance tokens, shuffled card decks, five-card Row, three Reserve stacks, shuffled human ten-card decks, random first player.

S02.passages: Phase 5 Recall: return Mentat, recall Agents and pass first-player marker before next round.

S03.passages: Draw a card; In Play; Mentat glossary (Mentat retention wording superseded by FAQ Sort Through the Chaos timing).

S04.passages: Sort Through the Chaos: take the Mentat at the start of the next round.

S05.passages: Foldspace acquisition restricted to Foldspace icon; Dispatch an Envoy preserves original icons and does not duplicate an existing icon; Intrigue cards delayed effects.

S06.passages: Acquiring Cards: five Row cards or Arrakis Liaison/The Spice Must Flow from Reserve; Foldspace Board Space Guide effect.

S07.passages: troops: supply-only recruitment; no re-recruiting garrison troops to evade deployment cap; on a Combat-space turn deploy troops recruited from any source, including Intrigue.

S08.passages: Deploying Troops to the Conflict: new recruits and up to two additional garrison troops; non-Combat Rally Troops example.

S09.passages: Recruitment Mission applies only during Reveal this round; draw-during-Reveal cards immediately revealed and used.

S10.passages: Deck Building: when unable to draw because deck is empty, reshuffle discard into a new deck and continue; Reveal cleanup moves Agent/Reveal cards to discard.

S11.passages: Every Board Space Guide entry, Sell Melange exchange diagram, complete general and two-player House Hagal rules.

S12.passages: Complete local FAQ extraction read; base-applicable entries reviewed.

coverage_challenge.result: The claim that two later passes found no meaningful additions is not sustained. Three high-confidence omitted base rules remain plus two procedural coverage gaps.
strongest_challenges: FAQ Foldspace is cited by the ledger but its only-icon acquisition restriction is never tested.
FAQ Dispatch an Envoy is entirely absent from the ledger and bank.
FAQ troops is cited against Q06 although Q06 omits any-source recruitment and the express no-re-recruiting exception.
additional_procedural_gaps: Normal empty-deck reshuffle and continued drawing are only adjacent to tested inspection/Refocus questions.
Initial shuffled human decks and initial Imperium/Intrigue/Reserve preparation are not asked despite the ledger claiming setup coverage.

coverage_challenge.limitations: No conclusion about omitted rules printed only on individual cards beyond the supplied rulebook and official FAQ; the audit uses the specified authoritative source set. Proposed additions are not inserted into the frozen bank.
